slices.focus: Comprehensive onboarding — personal, family, work, finances, health, and life goals
slices.summary: Derek introduces himself comprehensively: a 41-year-old journeyman wireman for IBEW Local 5 in Pittsburgh, recently pulled into part-time apprenticeship instruction and safety coordination. He details his family (wife Erin, two kids, brother Logan), ongoing housing renovation, chronic back issues, and his life goal of building a retention-focused apprenticeship training system that raises first-to-third-year retention above 80 percent. The conversation establishes his ISTJ personality, dry humor under pressure, and preference for straightforward practical communication.

slices.focus: Near-miss ladder incident triggers first-year safety review and informal leadership
slices.summary: A first-year apprentice nearly falls off an extension ladder during a winter lighting retrofit at Derek's job site. Derek documents the near-miss formally, which escalates to a tense training center debrief where veteran staff react defensively. He is informally tasked with reviewing first-year ladder and lockout-tagout instruction, representing a significant though unofficial role shift toward programmatic safety leadership. The incident sharpens his focus but also worsens his sleep as he replays the avoidable nature of the event.

Circulating a short outline to colleagues before the next meeting
Building measurable check-ins to evaluate pilot effectiveness
Managing Ron Belski's expected resistance to changes
Protecting the first-year apprentice from becoming a cautionary tale
